title: Birbal and the Three Questions
moral: God is everywhere and sees everything.

scenes.summary: Akbar asks three difficult questions in court.
scenes.text: One day, Emperor Akbar asked where God lives, which direction God faces, and what God does.
scenes.image_prompt: king asking deep questions in royal court, cartoon style

scenes.summary: No one in the court can answer the questions.
scenes.text: The courtiers were silent because they did not know the answers.
scenes.image_prompt: people looking confused in court, cartoon scene

scenes.summary: Birbal uses simple examples to explain.
scenes.text: Birbal brought milk and asked where butter was. Akbar said it was everywhere.
scenes.image_prompt: birbal showing bowl of milk to king, cartoon illustration

scenes.summary: Birbal explains God's presence and direction.
scenes.text: Birbal compared God to butter in milk and light from a lamp that spreads everywhere.
scenes.image_prompt: lamp glowing in all directions while birbal explains, cartoon

scenes.summary: Birbal answers all questions and impresses Akbar.
scenes.text: Birbal said God changes situations by making the weak strong and the strong weak. Akbar was impressed. God is everywhere and sees everything.
scenes.image_prompt: king praising birbal in court, cheerful cartoon style

story: One day, Emperor Akbar asked three questions: where God lives, which direction God faces, and what God does. No one could answer. Birbal explained using simple examples like butter in milk and light from a lamp. He said God is everywhere, faces all directions, and changes situations. Akbar was impressed with his wisdom.
